a prime target for our follow-up campaign with

notes: J1211 (SDSS J121150.27+143716.2) is the target sdB + K3V binary. The paper gives no independent catalog identifier for the K3V companion, so the system/primary is represented as one star. It is categorized as follow_up because the study is explicitly a follow-up of Tillich et al. (2011), who found J1211 most likely unbound (T:p2-b5); the present paper still calls it a halo hyper-velocity star candidate and states that an unbound orbit cannot be ruled out (T:p1-b7), while the bound probability is model-dependent (T:p6-b6).

SDSS J121150.27+143716.2: RA and Dec are not separately tabulated in the paper; they are decoded from the SDSS designation in T:p1-b7. The abstract (T:p1-b7) quotes 5.5 ± 0.5 kpc as the distance obtained from the SDSS-III spectrum, while Sec. 3 and Table 1 (T:p4-b10, T:p5-b0) give the spectroscopic distance as 5.4 ± 0.5 kpc; Sec. 5 (T:p6-b6) adopts 5.5 ± 0.5 kpc as the combined spectroscopic+photometric distance. I record 5.5 kpc with the combined-distance condition and 5.4 kpc with the spectroscopic condition. Bound probabilities are reported explicitly; no unbound probabilities are tabulated, and I did not compute their complements. The v_grf value at the last disk passage in Table 1 is not included because the requested quantities use the present-day state.
